notes: Conjecture true: after 3911 the next terms are R19 and R23; no term has 5..40 digits except R19, R23. Digits must be 1,3,7,9; for m in {7,11,13,37} (10^6 = 1 mod m) N and every swap mod m depend only on digit counts per position class mod 6, so a pruned enumeration of count vectors (sieve.c) leaves at most 8936 numbers per length up to 23 (24.7 million for 24..40), all eliminated by a composite swap except R19, R23 (stage2.py, stage2x.py; BPSW composite verdicts are proofs). Cross-checks: xcheck.py (pruning sound for n <= 10, all 4^n strings), brute.c (direct enumeration n <= 14). Lean: R19_term, R23_term (entry's definition via Nat.digits, Pratt certificates). Outside Lean: the nonexistence of other terms with 5..40 digits (computation only).

prior_art.note: Related absolute primes A003459 (Richert-type arguments) use all permutations, not single swaps.
